Copy candidate X word $61/$62 and Y $63 into player X $5C/$5E and Y $5D, then return carry clear.

Use the room's byte boundaries at $7789 to scan six-byte exit rectangles at $72A2. Mode bit six chooses the sign of eligible rectangle flags, and bit seven requests a query without moving the player. On a match retain its auxiliary byte in $9B and either return or route through its low-six-bit destination. With no match, commit candidate coordinates unless query mode suppresses it, then return carry set.

Use A as an index into this load four-byte route table, wrapping the part-end case at 28. Set room, X and Y, retaining a relative Y offset during flicflac; request room redraw and clear the staged sprite positions. A pending wave or the part-end index sets completion flags and redirects the route to zero.

Save the actor position, add signed velocities and refresh its bounds. Test horizontal and vertical geometry plus the actor's movement limits. On a blocked axis, restore its coordinate, refresh bounds and reverse that axis velocity; preserve successful movement on the other axis.
Take the pending progress amount from $C4 and enter the room-progress update at $B10F.

Add A to the room saturating progress byte and scan 8 seven-byte threshold event(s). For newly crossed thresholds, write the specified replacement byte through its pointer and optionally publish a status message. Preserve caller X.
Preserve player state $59 while invoking the geometry-hazard response at $B17D, then restore that state.

When $BF is negative, choose recoil direction, subtract ten score units and eight energy, clear the hazard marker and select forced motion. A matching progress-event pointer can also select a central warning message.
Store direction/mode A in $BD, set forced-motion count $BE to two and queue effect eight.

Check the interaction's attack-mask and persistent prerequisites, subtract the attack's low-six-bit damage from its retained strength and play a hit effect. A final hit sets its persistent flag, applies the room tile change, awards score/progress and starts a timed impact animation at the object's coordinates. Return carry set when the attack type is refused.

Scan this load 1 seventeen-byte moving-platform record(s), selecting the current room. Draw each platform, then fill its remaining vertical extension using 4-cell glyph/colour rows clipped to the playfield.
Walk the local moving-platform records and redraw current-room bodies without the extension-fill pass.

Compute the moving platform screen/colour destination from position and its authored offset. Position parity selects a frame with 4-cell rows; draw up to four rows, clipping every row to the playfield. This load indexed source operands select the glyph and colour bytes.

After four elapsed low ticks, scan 1 platform record(s) for the current room. Contact, character, flash and flicflac flags determine whether and which way it moves between its bounds. Patch three collision lines and redraw; a player standing on it receives the same Y displacement in position and staged sprite layers.
Render laser charge $17 and piston charge $18 in their two status-field positions through the shared numeric writer, preserving X.

Form the signed horizontal separation between the actor rectangle and the supplied rectangle by summing their left/right bounds and subtracting the other pair, retaining the intermediate carries on the stack. Return the low difference in Y and high difference in A.

After at least five low ticks, walk this room's state range. Opening states approach their target position; closing states approach zero. A closing door with a collision record checks the player and four actor rectangles, reopening and postponing its timer when blocked. Mark changed states for the display updater.

For each state whose redraw bit is set, clear that bit and read its eight-byte descriptor. Adjust linked wall-collision records for the current opening position, then draw the descriptor's glyph rows and colours. Certain types select a pattern from $6C36; fully open types either copy the neighboring cell or blank the row.

Offset 0 within state_target_positions ($B765-$B770). Twelve target opening positions indexed by room-state type. Room geometry preparation copies the selected value into the runtime target array at $1260.
Offset 0 within state_row_widths ($B771-$B77C). Twelve glyph-row widths indexed by state type. The changed-state renderer uses the selected width for its pattern offset and row-copy loops.
Select forward bitmap orientation and enter $B781 to stage a short impact at half-resolution X and Y supplied by the caller.

Refuse with carry set while $7F denotes an active projectile. Otherwise stage sprite zero at the supplied position, unpack image $5F into its cache, select colour/flags and scenery priority, and retain a nonzero low tick in $13BB for the four-tick expiry helper. Return carry clear.
Scan this room's state range. For a state with a nonzero timer and opening flag $40, compare elapsed low ticks with $96; once reached, request its closing path through $87B9.

When $7F is active, run the impact animation if phase $80 is nonzero; otherwise move the shot using its type and elapsed ticks, test screen/room/actor collisions and publish sprite slot zero. A vertical upward shot can change to the downward type after impact. Update its cached bitmap, colour and scenery priority before marking the slot ready.
Offset 0 within projectile_up_displacements ($B951-$B954). Four upward displacement magnitudes selected from elapsed low-tick count, capped by the projectile updater before lookup.
Offset 0 within projectile_down_displacements ($B955-$B958). Four downward displacement magnitudes, paired with the upward table and selected by projectile type.
Offset 0 within projectile_horizontal_displacements ($B959-$B95C). Four horizontal displacement magnitudes indexed by the projectile's capped elapsed-tick count.
Offset 0 within projectile_bitmap_indices ($B95D-$B962). Six sprite image indices indexed by projectile type: the paired horizontal, downward and upward direction variants.
Offset 0 within projectile_reflection_flags ($B963-$B968). Six reflection flags paired with the projectile image/type table at $B95D.

Offset 0 within projectile_impact_x_offsets ($B969-$B96E). Six half-resolution horizontal offsets added to the geometry-clamped projectile contact X when placing its short impact sprite. The projectile type selects the entry.
Offset 0 within projectile_impact_y_offsets ($B96F-$B974). Six vertical offsets added to the clamped contact Y when placing a projectile's short impact sprite, paired with $B969.

Copy candidate coordinates into the geometry workspace, derive horizontal direction from old versus candidate X and call the horizontal collision resolver. Copy any clamped result back to the candidate fields and retain the collision carry.
Copy current player coordinates into the geometry workspace, use facing for the scan direction and X for its collision-shape index, then enter $B9AB.

Form the supplied pose rectangle and select the left/right collision list from the incoming carry. On contact, retain an optional hazard flag/pointer, compensate for the facing-dependent pose offset and clamp the workspace X to the contact boundary. Return carry set for contact.

Copy candidate coordinates and the old player Y into the geometry workspace, run the vertical resolver and propagate clamped coordinates back. A hazardous contact records its direction/pointer; a downward contact can update the retained landing Y.

Set carry for the upward scan, copy current coordinates, choose shape X and use the common vertical collision path. A contact with the hazard flag records the player's opposite facing for its later response.
Clear carry for the downward scan and share the coordinate setup and common vertical geometry resolver at $BA5F.
Set bit seven on direction A in $BF and retain the current collision record's fourth-byte address in $C0/$C1 for the later player response.
Compare old Y $67 with candidate Y $66 to choose vertical scan direction, then enter the common rectangle resolver at $BA9A.

Build the workspace pose rectangle and scan floor or ceiling records according to the saved carry. Skip disabled persistent gates. Downward motion additionally checks that the old bottom was above the candidate surface. On contact, clamp Y using the pose offset, return its contact pointer in $A5/$A6 and return A zero for a floor or $FF for a ceiling, with carry set. No contact returns carry clear.

Take a shape index in A and read its shared descriptor through $1C48. Wait until the staged player slots are free, place layered bitmap pieces in sprite slots 5 and 6 using the player's position/facing, unpack their cache images and optional lower vertical images, and apply descriptor colours. A flagged descriptor can add a weapon piece in slot 7 unless $A0 suppresses it. Apply hit-flash colours and sprite-priority checks, handle the pending effect at $9E, then mark slots 5-7 ready for publication.
RTS ending the layered player renderer. The impact-horizontal table uses this address as a base for nonzero selectors; selector one reads the following byte at $BD29.
Horizontal offsets for impact selectors one through eighteen. Selector nineteen overlaps the first vertical-offset byte immediately afterward; the renderer reverses X offsets for facing.

Offset 0 within data_cont_be56 ($BD3B-$BD4E). Offset 0 in player_impact_vertical_offsets ($BD3B-$BE69). Vertical offsets selected by pending player effect $9E. The renderer adds the offset to player Y, creates the short-impact sprite and clears the pending selector. Its first byte also supplies the horizontal offset for impact selector nineteen through the overlapping horizontal lookup base.

Take a secondary bitmap index in A and sprite slot in X. Select its back cache from $16ED[X]-$03A0[X], read the secondary directory at $C71D and enter the shared packed-bitmap decoder. Preserve Y and return the slot index with carry set.
As the secondary bitmap decoder, but add two to the cache destination index before unpacking to choose the alternate clipped slice. This load secondary directory begins at $C71D.
Take main bitmap index X and destination cache index A. Form its directory-word pointer at $C621+2*X, preserve Y in $7B and enter the packed decoder at $BDA6.

Decode the selected directory word into 63 sprite bytes at $2800+64*A with I/O hidden. A zero high byte fills $FF; otherwise the low fifteen bits address a packed stream relative to $C621. $48 escapes a literal and $49-$4F emit one through seven zeros. $7C selects reflection, and directory bit fifteen selects bit or two-bit-group reversal. Restore Y and the processor port.
Low address byte of the forward packed-stream LDA at $BDE7. Decoder setup patches it and its high byte from the selected directory stream pointer.

High operand byte of this load forward packed-stream LDA, patched with the selected stream address. The loop accepts literals, $48 escaped bytes and one-through-seven-zero runs until it has written 63 bytes.
Low operand byte of the escaped-literal LDA at $BE04, patched together with the ordinary forward source.
High address operand byte of the escaped-literal LDA at $BE04. It is patched with the same source pointer as the ordinary forward packed-stream lookup.

Reflect each decoded three-byte sprite row: reverse the byte order through the stack and translate each byte through $1000 or $1100. Carry from the directory's high flag selects two-bit-group or single-bit reversal. Runs and escaped bytes use the same packed format as the forward decoder; stop after 63 destination bytes.
Low operand byte of the reflected stream LDY at $BE3E, paired with its patched high byte at $BE40.

High operand byte of the reflected packed-stream source lookup. Decoder setup patches it and the escaped-byte source together; the loop reverses three-byte rows and translates each byte through the selected reflection table.
Low operand byte of the reflected escaped-literal LDY at $BE75, paired with $BE77.
High operand byte of the escaped-literal LDY at $BE75, patched together with the ordinary reflected packed-stream source.
Low address byte of the reflection lookup at $BE79. Setup writes zero here and selects page $10/$11 through its high operand byte.
High byte of the lookup at $BE79, patched to $10 or $11 to select reversal of two-bit groups or individual bits. Each result is pushed while the decoder reverses the three-byte row.

Select this room four geometry groups from $6D62, $6DEE, $6EA6, $6F3A, retaining their pointers in $85-$8C. Find its descriptors among 8 eight-byte state records at $6C75, initialize their opening targets from the local type table and mark them for redraw. Store the matching record range in $99/$9A.

Compare the room's character-bank selector with $43. If a change is needed, request the blank display mode, wait for the VIC mode bits, exchange the old bank back and the new bank in. Set the three background shadows from the room palettes, build the animation slots and draw the tile map, then restore the character display shadow $1B.
Low bytes of the seven bank-boundary pointers. An exchange uses boundaries Y and Y+1 to obtain its source and byte count.
Offset 1 within charset_bank_pointer_low ($BF52-$BF58). Low bytes of the seven bank-boundary pointers. An exchange uses boundaries Y and Y+1 to obtain its source and byte count.
High bytes paired with the seven bank-boundary low bytes. Equal adjacent boundaries describe an empty allocation; room selectors identify the banks the game requests.

Offset 1 within charset_bank_pointer_high ($BF59-$BF5F). High bytes paired with the seven bank-boundary low bytes. Equal adjacent boundaries describe an empty allocation; room selectors identify the banks the game requests.

Exchange the active world-character prefix beginning at $0810 with the source bank selected through this load boundary tables. The adjacent boundary supplies the byte count. A repeated exchange restores both regions.

Mix the retained random byte, a byte through $2A/$2B and CIA1 timer A low with carry retained between additions. Preserve Y and advance the pointer. At page limit $C6, reseed its page to $66+(timer-low AND $1F) and its low byte from timer A high.

Move each displayed character-energy value toward its target in steps of four and redraw the corresponding bar glyphs. Blink low-energy portraits using the saved portrait glyph/colour buffers, and update their warning patterns. Quantize the Master's energy into its six-cell indicator and update central colour effects.

Offset 0 within data_cont_c29e ($C183-$C186). Offset 0 in master_portrait_blink_colours ($C183-$C2A1). Four colours indexed by ($3A AND $19) shifted and masked to two bits. The HUD updater writes the selected colour to nine central portrait cells when its tick and message-phase tests permit it.

Offset 0 within energy_bar_character_base_offsets ($C187-$C188). Two status-screen offsets $18 and $0C, indexed by character. The energy-bar writer adds one of these to its folded segment position and row offset before replacing a glyph.

Offset 0 within data_cont_c2a4 ($C189-$C198). Offset 0 in energy_bar_glyphs_a ($C189-$C2B3). Sixteen glyph choices for one energy-bar drawing path, indexed by the retained energy segment and update state.
Offset 0 within data_cont_c2b4 ($C199-$C1A8). Offset 0 in energy_bar_glyphs_b ($C199-$C2C3). Alternate sixteen-glyph energy-bar choices used by the other direction/edge of the HUD update.

Offset 0 within data_cont_c2c4 ($C1A9-$C1AC). Offset 0 in energy_bar_screen_row_offsets ($C1A9-$C2C7). Four row offsets $78,$50,$28,$00 used to place the character energy-bar segments in the status screen.
Offset 0 within data_cont_c2c8 ($C1AD-$C1C8). Offset 0 in low_energy_portrait_pattern_a ($C1AD-$C2E3). Twenty-eight warning glyphs written to a character portrait during its low-energy blink phase.
Offset 0 within data_cont_c2e4 ($C1C9-$C1E4). Offset 0 in low_energy_portrait_pattern_b ($C1C9-$C2FF). Twenty-eight warning glyphs for the other portrait's low-energy blink pattern.

Take tile index X, orientation Y and screen destination $1C/$1D. Write sixteen character indices in four rows of four cells and their colour nibbles to the corresponding colour-RAM cells. Zero orientation reads the normal glyph/colour planes; nonzero orientation reads the stored reflected planes. Each packed colour byte supplies a high-nibble and low-nibble cell pair.

Scan variable-length animation records at $6367 for the current room and allocate up to 24 slots. Each header supplies room, length/final flag, tile position and control, followed by two-byte tile/flag frames. Consider the final negative-length record before stopping and clear unused slots.

Work once per change of tick $3A. Walk 24 animation slots, apply the control byte's state gates through $02C0, start or advance the two-byte frame cursor when its delay expires, and draw the selected tile/orientation through $C1E5. Frame bit seven resets the sequence, bits one-five encode delay and bit zero selects reflection. A flagged frame can publish its sequence position into the corresponding state byte. After the slots, clear bit six on nonnegative state bytes.
Take room A and column-major tile position X. Locate its map at $3B2F+60*room, move six bytes per group of five tile positions and return tile in Y and reflection zero/one in A.
Compute $3B2F+60*room from $3C and return its pointer in $1A/$1B. A room record has ten columns, each with five tile numbers and one reflection-bit byte.

Select the room's conditional tile changes, compute its base map pointer and draw ten columns of five four-by-four tiles into the 40-by-20-cell playfield at $04C8. Column flag bits choose reflection. Enabled replacement records can substitute a tile and orientation at a grid position; disabled records leave the base map cell in place.

Advance the tile-change pointer at $20/$21 by four bytes and enter the search for the next enabled record at $C5F2.
